title: Vistra gets $4.2B DOE loan for planned uprates in Ohio, Pennsylvania
summary: Vistra is set to receive an approximately $4.2 billion loan from the Department of Energy to upgrade and uprate its fleet of nuclear reactors in Pennsylvania and Ohio, the DOE announced Monday. This work will add 433 MW of new nuclear capacity to help meet electricity demand in Pennsylvania, Ohio, and the 13-state PJM region, according to the DOE. It also will preserve 4 GW of existing baseload power and support roughly 3,000 engineering, construction, and planned outage jobs and thousands of other permanent jobs.

title: Nano Nuclear seeks to build front-end capabilities with Radnostix assets
summary: An image representing the intellectual property assets Nano seeks to acquire, which are associated with Radnostix’s previously planned Lea County, N.M., facility. (Source: Nano Nuclear) Nano Nuclear is continuing its efforts to establish itself in multiple sectors of the nuclear energy industry. On October 1, the company, which is perhaps best known for its efforts to deploy high-temperature gas-cooled microreactors, announced that it had agreed to purchase assets related to Radnostix Inc.'s previously planned deconversion facility in Lea County, N.M.

title: Details emerge on Valar’s Utah plans
summary: Last week, NPR reported that reactor start-up Valar Atomics is planning to construct a new facility in Utah that would feature 456 of its reactors. This campus, called Project Beehive, would sit on more than 9,000 acres of Bureau of Land Management land and would feature co-located data centers and a fuel production facility.
